utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Courtroom III, today. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Before we start, I inform the parties that Judge Fluegge for urgent tribunal matters is unable to continue to hear this case today. Judge Moloto and myself have decided it's in the interests of justice to continue to hear the case. The absence of Judge Fluegge will be limited in time within the -- apparently there is a problem with the interpretation. Is the translation okay now? Yes, it's confirmed. I see Mr. ... I see that Mr. Mladic is confirming and is nodding in the affirmative. It also seems that the e-court transcript issues have been resolved, but I interrupted myself when I said that the -- Judge Moloto and myself have decided it's in the interests of justice to continue to hear the case. Judge Fluegge is unavailable for today and tomorrow, if I understand him well, for urgent publicly known Tribunal reasons. The Chamber was informed that the Prosecution would like to raise a preliminary matter. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President. And good morning. I'm rising this morning just to confirm one procedural point regarding the upcoming Defence bar table motions. As Your Honours are aware, based on the scheduling information we received last week, we will not be in court when the motions are filed. Of course, we are in contact with the Defence, and trying to facilitate resolving the motions expeditiously. I have discussed the procedural point I'm raising now with Mr. Lukic and I was informed yesterday afternoon that the Defence didn't yet have a position on it. The Chamber' decision yesterday regarding the 92 bis motion for Jasmin Odobasic, and the Chamber's approach to additional portions of transcripts tendered with 92 bis and 92 quater witnesses reflects, in our view, a practical approach to adding necessary context to written evidence tendered by a party, by encouraging the parties to tender what they consider to be necessary contextualising material in their responsive filings. Our view is this maximizes efficiency and clarity of the record. We think a similar approach will assist us in focussing the issues in dispute in the litigation of the bar table motions themselves, and I understand that, for similar reasons, this approach has been taken in response to bar table filings in at least one closely related case. Our understanding based on case practice is that this is the approach the Chamber would prefer but because we won't be in court when the motions are filed, to facilitate litigating them quickly and efficiency we just ask the Chamber to confirm our understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will consider that in its full composition, Mr. Traldi. Therefore, we'll let you know soon. You were rather vague: "In another closely related case." Could you just say which case it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, doesn't surprise me, but ... Anything the -- well, if -- if there's anything the Defence would like to raise in this context we'd rather hear from the Defence -- well, before the start of the recess.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We'll do that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we have another technical problem to be resolved. Mr. Ivetic, is not in any way triggered by the Chamber to make speaking more difficult for you, but the microphone of Mr. Ivetic needs some attention in order to avoid that it again gives a lot of noise not produced by Mr. Ivetic. Then all technical problems being resolved, we'll hear from the Defence before the recess. And could we have the curtains down in order to allow the witness to enter the courtroom. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, I'd just ask to be excused with that matter having been dealt with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you are excused, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, just to alert the Chamber, I'm going to be proceeding this session without any direct LiveNote on my individual computer. That will be resolved during the next break. However, I will try to follow as best as I can on another screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I should have raised the matter because we were facing similar problems. Meanwhile, it has repaired for us. I take it would be soon. If it causes you any insurmountable problem, Mr. Weber, don't hesitate to address me. Yes, the curtains may be up again. Good morning, Witness GRM116. Before we continue, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the some declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. You'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Weber. You find Mr. Weber to your right. Mr. Weber is counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Weber, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness apparently draws my attention. Yes, is there anything you'd like to raise at this moment, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to apologise for the wrong date that I provided yesterday for the beginning of the war. My brain quite simply froze. This is a fact everyone knows, just like little children do, about the date of the war in Bosnia. So I would like to apologise to you and to the Defence if this caused any damage. I said it was in 1990 but everyone knows when it started.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there's no dispute about the -- among the parties, I think, about when the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina started. That it was 1992 rather than 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think there will be any dispute about this, and I think we can agree about this as we can about the documents that relate to the matter. And I would also like to thank the witness on this occasion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's proceed. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir -- good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: GRM116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, did you review your statement last night?

utterances.speaker: GRM116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, sir, is that how you came to the realisation that some of the information that you provided, whether it be dates and events, were not accurate yesterday?

utterances.speaker: GRM116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I realised that in the corridor. As far as the date is concerned, as far as my statements are concerned, they are all correct for certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The first time you testified was in the Karadzic case; correct?

utterances.speaker: GRM116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You decided to come forward in 2013 after you saw Mr. Petronijevic on TV discussing the Karadzic proceedings; right?

utterances.speaker: GRM116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was in 2013, but it was around that time, roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. We take a break, and we resume at ten minutes to 11.00, where we'll start -- Mr. Weber, can we start in open session?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think that the topic I'm going to go into right afterwards, although it was partially handled in open session in the direct examination, I think could trigger him providing personal information that could identify him, so if we could stay in private session just out of caution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll then immediately turn into private session once we have returned at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom. Once he has taken his seat, the curtains may be drawn up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And we already could move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nor is 72.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders the document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be MFI P7787.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 3355 -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When I said "admitted," I should have said marked for identification. Unless you would not insist -- it is mainly a list of names, Mr. Stojanovic. I don't know whether you on the -- I can read it says: "State delegation of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina on peace talks, Geneva, January 18, 1994," and then a name of -- a list of names follows. Signed by the Ambassador Mustafa Bijedic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no problem with the document. But I would just like to note that in the transcript it was not recorded completely the answer of the witness in B/C/S. And that is line 13. Page 53 of the transcript. And perhaps the witness could repeat what he said regarding the number of people.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should I say something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We briefly move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. We'll briefly have the curtains down, but we'll remain in open session immediately after the witness has left the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petronijevic, you're excused as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRONIJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that's -- perhaps we should have instructed the usher to bring the previous witness, which is then continuing now his -- to the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, with the Chamber's permission, if myself and Mr. Kimberley can be excused, and we'll change over the seats.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you inform the Chamber. There was some matter about -- to be discussed with the Prosecution about, I think, how to introduce perhaps factual documents without necessarily seeking the opinion to the extent it would be outside the scope of the expertise of the witness. Could you first inform us about the result of that. And, second, could you tell us how much time you would still need.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that I shorten my time by proposing to the Prosecution and we informed the Chamber some documents we would offer without calling them up on our screens. And I don't know the answer yet because we didn't have time to see if Mr. MacDonald agrees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll hear from him. But let's first welcome the witness into the courtroom. Mr. Pavlovic, please be seated. I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by your solemn declaration. Mr. Lukic, since the chair now seems to be in the right position to testify, but could you give us -- let's just assume that Mr. MacDonald -- yes, Mr. MacDonald would accept your invitation, how much time would you still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] two and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll consider whether we'll grant you that portion in time. I mean, it's all the way in which you presented the expert report. Try to speed up but let's see how things happen. Mr. MacDonald, how much time you would need?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: We're still on two hours for cross-examination but I wonder if Your Honour wanted to hear back about the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, also.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I am afraid that the Prosecution won't be agreeing, certainly not wholesale, to this list Your Honour. In essence, we have a running list of objections, for example, we found seven without translations so far, which we are still trying to get through to process. We found one witness who seems to be on the Defence's list of witnesses to call; that's GRM241. I don't know if my friend planned to be dropping that witness or not. But this would be an inappropriate way to introduce his evidence if Defence was still trying to call him as well. Your Honour will see as a third category there are three statements which are not referred to in the report and to come in without reference to the report without any testimony on these documents, in essence, it's a bar table motion rather than anything else, Your Honour. And the first one, in particular, the testimony from the Karadzic case, we would object to that coming in untested, Your Honour, certainly. I can't say that's a full list of objections yet, Your Honour. I am afraid we only got this this morning. But that's what we have so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The first one was mistakenly there and I checked that we cannot offer without calling this document up, the first one from the list. It's 1D06267.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that used for the witness to draw any conclusions?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you should have thought about that when tendering the expert report. At least you know now of some of the -- of some of the objections. Could you already please keep that in mind. Continue your conversations with Mr. MacDonald. And also keep in mind that if you present this material without translation, that that's, of course, not the way to proceed. Please proceed, and as I earlier said, we -- the Chamber is really insisting on finishing the evidence of this witness this week. We'll have to find a solution. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would quote which documents just for identification when we reached them in our questions. And, first of all, I forgot to offer into evidence used two days ago at transcript page 42637, line 13, and it's the document 1D06269.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. The only thing I would add is this is referenced in the report and the reason I say that is there is a partial translation of the part that my friend read out which I'm not sure he took you to on Monday. I had the footnote. I can't find it right now, but I will endeavour to find it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it will be marked for identification for the time being. Mr. Registrar, 1D06269 would receive number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D1391, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Marked for identification. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And the last document in relation to Kamenica area we would offer -- give me just one second. 1D06326. That one is translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I've not heard yet of any objections. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D1392, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. D1392 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day. And I would like to wish good day to everyone in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I neglected you a little bit because of some technical matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have on our screens, please, 1D06262, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're going to see the document in just a little bit. We now see it on the screen. This is the Agency for Investigation and Documentation, AID, sector Tuzla, dated the 1st of February, 1996. A record of his statement was made; it's a statement by Suljo Halilovic. In the statement, we need to see the first page that we're seeing on the screens now. We need to look at paragraph 2 in the B/C/S version and paragraph 3 of the English version. It begins with: "Near Kamenica, before the asphalt road reading from Konjevic Polje to Nova Kasaba in the village of Kaldrmica, fire from Praga self-propelled anti-aircraft gun was opened." And then it goes on to say: "In my estimation about 1.000 people were killed as a consequence of the Chetnik attack." Which area was this?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an area between Kamenica that we also discussed the previous day, where there were a lot of victims, and the Konjevic-Nova Kasaba road. So there's a distance of about 5 or 6 kilometres between these two points. And it says that this was before the asphalt road in the Kaldrmica village. That's where the 28th Division was withdrawing. So that would, roughly speaking, be the location mentioned by the witness who gave a statement to Mr. Ruez. When we were referring to Burnice -- Kamenica, Burnice, [indiscernible] and the road that I have already mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you assist me in telling me where we were in the report at this moment. Focussing on what?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's 55H.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At the same time, we're close to the moment, if not yet at the moment where we should take a break. I leave it in your hands whether you have one or two questions left or you take the break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can use two or three minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This area, Kaldrmica, is it a different area from Kamenica?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Kamenica is above Kravica and Sandici from that point to Kaldici to the Konjevic Polje-Nova Kasaba road. Well, there is a bridge over the Jadar there, and the units of the 28th Division withdrew at that point. I said the distance between those points was 5 or 6 kilometres as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would tender this document into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 1D6262 will be Exhibit D1393, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Two more documents in relation to this location. The first one is 1D06328, translated, and we would ask that one to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's Exhibit D1394, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then the next one is 1D06320, not translated yet. We would propose it to be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D1395, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And we are ready for the break now, Your Honour, if it suits you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll take a break. Mr. Pavlovic, it was rather short, but we'll continue in 20 minutes from now. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at 20 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. MacDonald, could we already ask the usher to escort the witness into the courtroom because there was a preliminary matter. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Just a short one, Your Honour. The last document that was put forward for admission which I believe is MFI D1395, I misread my notes. The Prosecution would object to that on the basis that we don't know what it says yet and it's not referenced in the report. It is MFI'd already, but just to put that on the record, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So for an additional reason, it's now MFI'd. Please proceed, once the witness has taken his seat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Because of this, obviously we have to go back. If we can have D1395 MFI on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Pavlovic, this document hasn't been translated and it's not referred to in the report. This is additional documentation. So there is something I will ask you now. As you can see, it is a document from the security sector of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the 2nd Corps command, dated the 10th of October, 1995, signed by the assistant commander for security, Colonel --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zivic [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ziljic, Mehmed. It's Mevludin Hrlic's statement, Hanjic Mevludin's [as interpreted] statement. If we could have a look at the second page, please. We need the last 17 lines on this page. You say this also would occur -- or, rather, in the column, there were people who would die. They'd probably been stabbed but it was difficult to identify the perpetrator. They say that the column was -- they waited for the column in Kamenica, about 1800 hours on the 12th of July, 1995. "We lined up when fire was suddenly opened from all sides. And people were falling all over. Chemical weapons were also used and people were rendered mad by this so they even killed each other with their own personal weapons and grenades. They also opened fire on anyone they would see so the slaughter there was one of the worst slaughters ever. I went down Pobudje with a group of people to the canyon that river Kravica and we were ambushed again there, and on that occasion, about 100 individuals died. Then I arrived in the village of Krajinovici and there were a lot of people that I saw there. We then moved down the asphalt road to Konjevic Polje or, rather, to Kaldrmica. The Chetniks were waiting for us again there and they opened fire on that mass. And on that occasion, many individuals were killed or wounded." Which area are we referring to here, Mr. Pavlovic, could you please assist us.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The witness, the eye-witness to the events in the first part that you have read out is speaking about the events at Kamenica and is repeating things that we have already discussed. Reference is made to large-scale combat, widespread panic, to the fact that people are fighting amongst themselves because there was panic and fear. There were -- there was a significant number of victims, and the second part that you read out refers to the area that the previous eye-witness also mentioned, the witness whom we have already discussed. This is the Krajinovici area from Kamenica onwards towards Kamenica and the Konjevic Polje-Nova Kasaba road. So between Kasaba and that road, the distance is about 5 or 6 kilometres. It is 2 or 3 kilometres from Kamenica and it's perhaps about 1 kilometre from the road. Roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have document 1D06255, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the Chamber is fully puzzled by what you're doing at this moment. I mean, what you're doing is you put a statement to the witness which is not apparently used in his expert report. You ask him to interpret that statement and that's it. And more or the less of the whole of the gist of what happens is that you invite this witness to reconstruct the facts on the ground. He is called as an expert for totally different matters, and it is for this Chamber to evaluate all of the evidence which is before it. This witness doesn't, at this moment, add that much to it. If it says Kamenica in the one and Kamenica in the other, then we could expect that it's the same. But this is all in the context of the witness telling us what happened. It's for the Chamber to decide what happened, on the basis of all the evidence before it, and not to adopt or follow an expert who is not called an expert on the matters involved. To adopt any of his conclusions on the materials he apparently has used or sometimes not even used in his report, we totally are puzzled by that. I hope you understand that and keep that in mind, if you continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Particularly in the light -- in light of the fact, Mr. Lukic, that you now reading from this document after Mr. MacDonald has stood up to say he is objecting to it because he doesn't know what it means.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's why I went back because it was MFI'd already [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just those questions doesn't make it any more admissible. You say this witness is seeing the document for the first time today and then he's giving us an interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, it's not an interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But it's not in his report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's additional documents that he provided us with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's not in his report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This one is not in his report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But still describes the same events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well, having not access to the whole of the document, of course, I'm not inviting you to read the whole of it, but you select portions just as the witness selected documents and that apparently, at least that's what I assume, is that you expect this Chamber to adopt the same conclusions on a different set of materials, not necessarily all the other materials included, and then adopt conclusions which are not within the scope of the expertise of this witness. Because this witness is not a expert in evaluating evidence on what happened on the ground, yes or no. He is an expert in the fields for which is he presented as an expert. Please proceed, and, again, try to keep in mind both my observations and those of Judge Moloto.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. But the work of this witness is "Analysis of losses incurred by the 28th Division of B and H Army during the breaking through from" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the title. You asked him to write about it. His expertise is explained in a different way. And his expertise does not include drawing conclusions on events that may have happened on the basis of personally selected materials by this witness rather than on the basis of the evidence before this Chamber. Rightly so, because we'll have to do that job. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have 1D06255, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I was just warned that it's actually D1379, what I'm looking for.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While we are waiting, this is a document from the federal Ministry of Defence, the security sector, and the sector for intelligence affairs. It's the details of the events and the activities of certain individuals preceding the fall of Srebrenica. 51B, 55Y, 97B, 62Dz, are the footnotes that also refer to this document. It's been partially translated. We need to see the 14th page in the B/C/S version, and in the English version --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please repeat the page reference. Page 2 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the B/C/S version, it's in the middle of the page. It refers to an area on to the column. In the English version, it's the first paragraph, nine lines from the bottom. From the last line in the first paragraph. Nine lines towards the top, in fact. It says in the earlier -- evening hours in the Ljesina area, the Nova Kasaba-Konjevic Polje area was secured and it says that there were groups of about 100 who started crossing over through the road. And then it say there is was an intense -- an intense artillery and infantry attack launched against the column at that time. Now I'd move onto page 15 in the B/C/S version, page 15, the second part of the second paragraph. And in the English version, it's page 3, the sixth line from the bottom of the page. It says: Mujic Besic [as interpreted] from the Kamenica area ran into Dzemal Topic with another 15 people. They saw about 1.000 dead Bosniaks next to the asphalt. Mujic saw an [indiscernible] for a freshly dug mass grave that had not been properly covered and there was an unpleasant smell. A little further below, it says what Dzemal Hasanovic stated. It says: In his testimony, he stated that in the immediate vicinity of Konjevic Polje he was an eye-witness to when Chetniks fired tank shells at the column from very close range and in his estimate on that occasion they killed over 500 Bosniaks in this way. The corpses of these victims were transported all night in trucks in a direction he was unaware of. What is the location that we are referring to here, Mr. Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the Nova Kasaba-Konjevic Polje road, which is very important because there were large-scale battles there and large-scale losses. The first witness or eye-witness speaks about the area nearer to Nova Kasaba because he talks about Dzugum, the settlement of Dzugum. He had saw 1.000 Bosniaks that had been killed by the very asphalt. The other witness mentioned an area in the immediate vicinity of Konjevic Polje. From Nova Kasaba and Dzugum, it is at a distance of a few kilometres, and in his estimate he saw over 500 Bosniaks who had been killed on that occasion, and their corpses were taken away in trucks, I assume, so as to make the road practicable again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll ask you about the mass grave later referred to by this witness and also I'll ask you about the bodies that were driven away. This document has already been admitted. We would like to refer to the document referred in the footnote 62C. We'd like to tender it. 1D06235.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If it is the statement by Nedzad Ademovic, I seem to recall that it was tendered already, although I'd very to check. Perhaps not. I know it's been used before, I'm pretty sure.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D1378, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I stand corrected. Sorry. And we would just mention in connection with this, the document mentioned in footnote 62C, with two diacritics, it's already admitted as P03378.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me ask you this: How is it that in your work on the basis of these documents you found that, while crossing the road and in the breakthrough, only 700 members of the column were killed?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must tell you that because of my professional experience and training and the education I went through in Yad Vashem in Israel, I adopt a conservative approach, while estimating the victims. I said at least 700. Perhaps there were more. What I did here was that I proceeded on the assumption that some witnesses, because this is an area of some 2 kilometres of the road, perhaps did not see the same bodies, and also perhaps they --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just one moment. Did you say they did not see or that they did see the same bodies?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That they did see perhaps the same bodies. Because the first witness speaks about Dzugum near Nova Kasaba, the other one talks about a location near Konjevic Polje so perhaps he doesn't know that terrain sufficiently. Perhaps it looked to him as if there were more than there actually were. So I proceeded with a large dose of caution when I stated this number and then I took the numbers of another eye-witness who spoke about 200 killed while crossing the road near Sandici. So I cited that number for all of those reasons. I did the same thing while estimating the first part of the breakthrough. So as an expert in this segment of my work when we're making a reconstruction in order to be able to know where we should look for somebody, that is my approach, and I stand by it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, is there any reason why the 200 could not be the accurate number?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I think that I already explained, that I allow for the possibility that certain witnesses saw the same group of those killed or at that point in time perhaps it could have seemed to them because they were seeing it as it was happening, that due to panic or fear that it seemed to them as if they were seeing more. So on the basis of some other statements that I saw, sometimes even 1700 were mentioned. But that is not my approach. My approach is very conservative. I'm trying to look at all the circumstances, when something happened, how it happened, when the witness saw it, did he see it as it was happening or a couple of weeks later, as we had also witnesses. So that's how it was. I hope that I have helped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question is if one witness says 200 and another says 1700, why would it be 700 -- I do understand that you didn't take the maximum, you find somewhere in the middle. Why not take the minimum, 200. I mean, what's in your expertise which tells you, apart from just weighing a bit that evidence which is not, I think, your specific expertise, but, it's, rather a task for this Court, why don't you say, well, one says 200, could be 200.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I said 200, I meant a completely different location near Sandici. As the crow flies that is some 5 or 6 kilometres farther away. It doesn't refer to this other particular section of the road. It's kilometres away from that area. So the witness is speaking about 200 being killed while crossing the road in Sandici. This is a different section. We didn't read that statement but it's quoted in my work. So I took two lowest estimates, two lowest numbers. I have to be cautious here, and I cannot just give any general evaluations. I have to have certain parameters that I'm using in my work and in my methodology.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you are saying the 200 is about a totally different location is therefore totally irrelevant for your assessment. Nevertheless you mentioned that as an element in being very cautious. I have difficulties in understanding how that works, but ... Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are these 200 irrelevant or did you take them into account?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not something that can be irrelevant. Had it been irrelevant, I would not have included that in my work --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the last sentence which was not heard.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my work, I tried to find statements by eye-witnesses that I believed had a certain weight and relevance because of who provided them and when they provided them. The statement by the eye-witness who said that 200 were killed between the 12th and the 13th while crossing the Sandici road is a statement that possesses relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... yes. That's apparently is not a repetition of the last sentence. Now, one of the answers asked about the relevance of the 200 is -- that's not something that can be relevant and then an answer to the next question you say the statement by the eye-witness who said that 200 were killed between the 12th and the 13th while crossing the Sandici road is a statement that possesses relevance. I'm lost. And I asked you about it because it was part of your answer when you explained how cautiously were approaching the matter, you specifically mentioned the 200 as an element which caused you to be very cautious so I'm -- it's unclear it me, let's me say that at this moment but I don't know whether the same is true for my colleagues but at least for you to know, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are operating on the basis of interpretation --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, I didn't hear the entire question because of the overlapping speech and interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Sorry, today is cabin behind me so I cannot follow. [Interpretation] Today, since we're working on the basis of interpretation, today, did you ever say today in your testimony that these 200 were irrelevant?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think that I did not say that the statement or that the number were irrelevant. I said that they were relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And one more thing that I noticed. Did you ever said that in one statement you said that somebody referred to 1700?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I did not say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What did you say what do you think when you mentioned the number 1700?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I wanted to say was that if I were to automatically add up or make general conclusions, then I could come to a conclusion that it was 1700. However, my approach is different, and I already explained that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And these 700, are they from the same location that you found or were they from different locations?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These 700 include those bodies that were seen on the section of the road Konjevic Polje-Nova Kasaba and 200 in the section of the road near Sandici, and these two locations are some 5 to 7 kilometres apart.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your microphone was not activated. But I could imagine that you were drawing my attention to the fact that it is a quarter past 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Pavlovic, we'll adjourn for the day. We'll resume tomorrow. I will discuss for one second with the parties how to proceed tomorrow, but you are already allowed to follow the usher, but not until after you have confirmed that you understand my instruction that you should not speak or communicate in whatever way, with whomever, about your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, has the last break resulted in any further update on how to proceed? Because tomorrow this Chamber thinks that it is -- it's fully in line with a fair trial that we should conclude hearing the testimony of this witness tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is genocide count in our indictment and we don't think that we should be rushed in any way. We really have to go with this expert through certain documents and we would offer another for admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, apparently it escaped your mind what we said again and again and again, that is, that the existence of such statements do not in any way allow, within the scope of the expertise of this witness, to draw the kind of conclusions he draws, and we urged you again and again and again to focus on what the expertise of this witness is. Now, if he, in his daily work, pays attention to background offered to him and he draws any conclusions on that, that's his sake. But he's here presented as a witness in a certain field, and most of the exercise he makes is beyond that field of expertise. We have emphasised that again and again. You are invited to seek agreement with Mr. MacDonald how to proceed in such a way tomorrow that we can conclude the evidence of this witness. If not, the Chamber will set time limits. Just for your information. We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume tomorrow, the 17th of December, 9.30 in the morning, and I think we are back in courtroom 1 tomorrow. We are. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 17th day of December, 2015, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.20 p.m.,
